lines: Mind the crate. It's been there four months and it'll be there four more.
You'll be the one from the gallows.
Prices are on the shelf. Same as they are for everybody.

choices.text: Let me see what you have.

lines: You were sentenced. You weren't convicted of not paying.
I'm not doing you a kindness. I'm doing arithmetic.
No. I was here. Somebody has to be, or the door's shut when they come back needing rope.
I'm not telling you that to look better than them. I'd probably have gone.
Everyone else did. That's what a crowd is — it's not a decision, it's the absence of one.
So no. I don't get to be the good one. I get to be the one who was busy.
It's cheap. Honesty always is when it's about something you didn't do.
Right. Food, rope, a salve if you've been careless.
I'll take most things off you. Not everything — I've a shop, not a midden.

choices.text: What's your father's name doing on the sign?

lines: TALLOW AND SON. My father painted it before he had children, which tells you what he was expecting.
He got me. Then he got a son, and the valley got him, and I got the shop.
I've not repainted it. Everybody knows where the shop is.
You didn't do it. Don't stand in my shop apologising for the weather.
But — thank you. Noted and filed.
It's a *painted* sign. It's not good or bad, it's just up.
...it is a good sign.
Since you ask. The carters stopped coming through in the spring.
Half my shelf comes up the south road, and the south road is where you've been going.
Bring me things and I'll pay over the odds for them. Not charity — I've nobody else to buy from.
Anything the valley still makes. Anything you'd eat and not regret.
I'll know it when I see it, and I'll tell you what it's worth before you hand it over.
Good. That's an arrangement, not a favour.
Come back with a full pack and we'll both have had a decent day.
Back. Still standing, still solvent.
Shelf's where it was.

choices.text: Let me see what you have.
You said you needed things brought up.
What's your father's name doing on the sign?

lines: I did. I still do. That's the trouble with the arrangement — it doesn't finish.
Empty the pack out and I'll tell you what's worth having.
Then you've come a long way to tell me so.
Go on. South road. Mind the crate on your way out.
